toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B looks fine. The single Level 2 potassium flag is most likely a chance outlier, since about one or two a month are expected. A possible sampling glitch can't be ruled out, and it makes no difference to what you do. The repeat passed. Levels 1 and 3 and sodium and chloride were fine. Level 2 averages are unchanged after the lot change. Re-running 43 patient samples on Analyzer A matched within 0.02 on average. The patient median is stable. All scheduled QC ran on time, so the claim that short staffing led to skipped QC isn't supported.

Ward 6's high potassiums are split 7 on A and 7 on B. They coincide with the tube outage and four renal overflow patients. Long transit times are more common among the high results (11 of 14), which fits delayed samples, but this isn't proven.

Sign off: return B to service, with no recall, no lot quarantine and no widened limits. Widening limits would blunt a working control. A recall would mean recollecting about 2,900 patients for no good reason. Consider an extra Level 2 QC each shift for a week. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples on the high results. Get the tube fixed. Tell Dr Larkby the analyzers are not giving false highs. I'm fairly confident, though I collected no further evidence.
